fields.text: A GLM builder writes an 11-line terrarium plan from a brief - 5 layers in bottom-to-top order, then 6 contents with exact counts - a second GLM turns the plan into a photo brief, and Muse renders the finished jar. Then the loop closes: a Gemini vision checker inventories only what is actually visible through the glass, layer by layer and item by counted item, a GLM auditor scores the plan against that inventory - present, missing, extra, layers in order or not - and a Decide judge labels the build built to plan, layers out of order, pieces missing or extras snuck in. The render has to answer to the plan. Four model families, four different jobs. See recipes/terrarium-build-audit.md.

nodes.name: Terrarium build, layer-checked - plan, render, read back, audit

fields.text: A low-maintenance desktop terrarium in one large open round glass jar for a bright office desk. Dry, sandy, desert-meets-coast look: pale layers, one small sculptural centrepiece plant, nothing that needs misting. Hard constraints: no animals, no figurines, no coloured sand art patterns, nothing plastic, and every layer must stay clearly visible through the glass.

fields.system: You are a meticulous terrarium builder. The input is a brief for one open glass-jar terrarium. Write ONE build plan in this exact shape: exactly 11 lines, numbered 1 to 11. Lines 1 to 5 are the LAYERS, bottom to top, each naming the material and its colour (for example '1. Layer: coarse cream gravel'). Lines 6 to 11 are the CONTENTS planted or placed on top, each with an exact count between 1 and 6 and a colour or material (for example '7. Contents: 3 small green fern fronds'). Every content item must be a distinct physical thing that can be seen through glass in a photograph - no animals, no text, no labels, nothing hidden under the soil. Honour every hard constraint in the brief. Output the plan only, no preamble, no closing remarks.

nodes.name: Build plan - GLM designs the terrarium

fields.system: You direct product photography. The input is a numbered terrarium build plan of 11 lines: 5 layers then 6 contents with exact counts. Output ONE image prompt, under 120 words, for a photograph of the finished terrarium: name every one of the 5 layers in bottom-to-top order and every one of the 6 contents exactly once with its exact count and colour, inside one large open round glass jar on a light wooden desk, bright window daylight, layers clearly visible through the glass, no people, no hands, no animals, no text, no labels, nothing in the frame that is not in the plan. Output the prompt only.

fields.question: The text is an 11-line terrarium build plan: 5 layers bottom to top, then 6 contents with exact counts. The image is a rendered terrarium that claims to follow exactly that plan. Which verdict fits? 'built to plan' means every layer is present in the planned order and every content item is visible at its planned count, with nothing unplanned added. 'layers out of order' means all 5 layers are present but at least one sits in the wrong position in the stack. 'pieces missing' means at least one planned layer or content item cannot be found (and the layers present are in order). 'extras snuck in' means everything planned is visible but one or more unplanned items also appear. Judge the build, not the photography.
fields.options:
built to plan
layers out of order
pieces missing
extras snuck in

fields.q: You are the bench checker in a terrarium pipeline. Look at this photograph of a glass-jar terrarium and report ONLY what you can actually see. First list the visible layers from bottom to top, one per line, each with its material and colour. Then list every visible plant or placed object, one per line, each with its colour and an exact count. Do not guess at anything hidden below the soil or behind glass glare - if you are unsure of an item, give your best guess and mark it '(?)'. Do not compare it to any plan; just report what is visibly there.

nodes.name: Bench check - Gemini reads the jar

fields.system: You are a terrarium auditor. The input gives a numbered build plan of 11 lines (lines 1-5 layers bottom to top, lines 6-11 contents with exact counts), then the marker 'VISIBLE IN THE TERRARIUM:' and an inventory of what a checker could actually see in the rendered terrarium. Compare the two, line by line. Output one line per planned line, in plan order, starting 'PRESENT - ' if a matching layer or item is visible (for contents, the read-back count must equal the planned count exactly) or 'MISSING - ' if it is not, followed by the line's short name. Then one 'EXTRA - ' line for each visible layer or item that is not in the plan, if any. Then one line 'Layers in order: yes' if the read-back lists the 5 layers in the same bottom-to-top order as the plan, otherwise 'Layers in order: no'. End with one line 'Summary: X of 11 present.' Judge by identity, colour and count; a close colour match counts as present. Output the audit only, no preamble.
